Population-averaged counterfactual contrast at a common session

Source: R/utils-marginal.R
marginal_contrast.Rd

For each posterior draw, predicts the expected outcome of n_new new cases drawn from the fitted random-effect distribution at follow-up session \(B\), once with treatment introduced just after session \(A\) and once without treatment, and averages over the new cases. The result is the population-averaged (marginal) treatment contrast at a single session, in contrast to the typical-case (conditional) contrasts of summarize_fixed_effect_decisions() and compute_phase_contrast(), which hold random effects at zero. On a log or logit link the two differ whenever random effects are present, because the mean of \(\exp(\cdot)\) over cases is not \(\exp(\cdot)\) at the mean case.

Usage

marginal_contrast(
  model,
  data = NULL,
  time_var = NULL,
  case_var = NULL,
  time_A = NULL,
  time_B = NULL,
  n_new = 200,
  ndraws = 500,
  intervention_goal = c("increase", "decrease"),
  ab_rule = c("scdhlm", "shortest_treatment"),
  duration = NULL
)

Arguments

model

A fitted brmsfit from an AB or multiple-baseline design.

data

The processed data the model was fitted to (with level_AB and time_A); defaults to model$data.

time_var

Time column; defaults to find_time_var(), and time_A is used when neither is present.

case_var

Case column; defaults to find_case_var().

time_A, time_B

Last pre-treatment session \(A\) and follow-up session \(B\) on the time scale of time_var; NULL uses the defaults in Details.

n_new

Number of new cases averaged per draw.

ndraws

Number of posterior draws.

intervention_goal

"increase" or "decrease"; sets the direction counted by prob_improvement.

ab_rule

"scdhlm" or "shortest_treatment"; the default rule for \(B\) (see Details).

duration

Optional \(B - A\) in sessions; overrides ab_rule.

Value

A list with

summary

Data frame with columns quantity, median, lower, upper (2.5\ quantiles) for mean_untreated, mean_treated, difference (treated minus untreated), ratio (treated over untreated; log links only), and prob_improvement, the posterior probability that the difference lies in the intervention_goal direction (given in median, with NA bounds).

draws

Data frame with one row per draw: draw, mean_untreated, mean_treated, difference, and ratio (log links only).

n_draws

Number of finite draws the summary uses.

time_A, time_B

The sessions used.

Details

The treated row uses the package's AB and multiple-baseline coding (see process_scd_phases()): time_A = B - T_A, with \(T_A\) the earliest first baseline session, level_AB = 1, and trend_AB = B - T_B, with \(T_B\) the first observed session after \(A\) (the treatment onset). The untreated row has time_A = B - T_A, level_AB = 0, and trend_AB = 0. A time_B column is B - T_B in both arms, as process_scd_phases() codes it on every row. Maintenance and generalization terms are 0. Each new case borrows one fitted row drawn at random, shared by its two arms, so predictors outside the design coding average over their observed distribution instead of being fixed at one row. A phase column (for example in sigma ~ phase) takes a baseline-role label in the untreated arm and an intervention-role label in the treated arm. Every grouping factor of the model, including an observation-level random effect, is relabeled to a new level per new case, so brms::posterior_epred() draws it with allow_new_levels = TRUE, sample_new_levels = "gaussian", and re_formula = NULL; both arms of a new case share its draw.

Autocorrelation. Predictions use incl_autocor = FALSE: the AR(1) residual has mean 0, so the expected outcome of a new case does not depend on lagged residuals, and the outcome values of the template rows never enter. On a log link with latent AR(1) residuals (non-Gaussian families in brms), covariance mode (cov = TRUE) uses stationary latent variance \(\sigma_e^2 / (1 - \phi^2)\), with sderr = \(\sigma_e\). Conditional mode (cov = FALSE) instead adds an independent latent residual and its lagged contribution: \(z_t + \phi z_{t-1}\), with independent \(z_t\) of variance \(\sigma_e^2\). Its interior-session variance is \(\sigma_e^2 (1 + \phi^2)\); at the initial session, the absent lag contributes zero and variance is \(\sigma_e^2\). The follow-up contrast uses the interior-session variance. Each draw is multiplied by the exponential of half the mode-specific variance. Unknown modes, higher AR orders, and MA terms are rejected rather than assigned this AR(1) correction. Other non-identity links hold the latent residual at 0 and warn. Draws with a non-finite contrast are NA in draws, excluded from summary, counted by n_draws, and reported in a warning.

Times. \(A\) is the last session of the shortest baseline across tiers. With ab_rule = "scdhlm" (default) \(B - A\) is the treatment duration of the tier(s) with that shortest baseline, as in scdhlm::default_times(); with "shortest_treatment" it is the shortest treatment duration across tiers. Tiers without both baseline and treatment sessions are left out. duration sets \(B - A\) directly, for a common benchmark duration across studies; time_B overrides both. Only AB and multiple-baseline (multiple-probe) fits carrying level_AB, trend_AB, and time_A are supported.

No established population-averaged estimand for single-case designs exists yet; this function follows the general counterfactual marginalization over new cases.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
  d <- process_scd_phases(simulate_scd_data(n_cases = 4), list(), "AB")
  fit <- build_model(d, "outcome ~ time_A + level_AB + trend_AB + (1 + level_AB | case)",
                     family = "poisson")
  marginal_contrast(fit, d)$summary
}
